program: Civil legal aid for housing, safety, benefits and economic security
priceScope: Conditional annual whole-recipient cost divided by a limited modeled local channel; not a verified marginal gift offer or complete portfolio EV

what: Lone Star Legal Aid provides free civil legal assistance to eligible low-income people in Texas and southwest Arkansas.
It handles housing, family safety, public benefits, consumer, disaster and employment matters.
Our deep model examines a conditional housing-health and household-resource channel, including full client burdens and distinct payer losses.
strengths: Legal barriers can affect both health and net household resources.
Matched 2024 recipient finances and case categories support a coherent annual reference.
Controlled legal-aid evidence and eviction research clarify mechanisms, alternatives and signed financial incidence.
reservations: Cases, categories and individuals are not deduplicated completed representation or causal successful households.
The reported economic awards and savings are not causal net consumption or all new government benefits.
Houston share, additional outcomes and health effects are unmeasured hypotheses; marginal donation response is unknown.

sections.what: Lone Star Legal Aid provides free civil legal assistance to eligible low-income people in Texas and southwest Arkansas. It handles housing, family safety, public benefits, consumer, disaster and employment matters. Our deep model examines a conditional housing-health and household-resource channel, including full client burdens and distinct payer losses.
sections.monitoring: The matched 2024 report records 25,111 cases, 61,289 individuals, 12,400+ housing cases and $15.3M awards/savings. Current 2025 homepage records 27,973 cases, 67,153 individuals, 6,099 housing cases and $12.69M awards/savings. Differences in definitions/vintages are not demonstrated effectiveness changes. No newer audited 2025 cost is imported. Request Houston unique households, service intensity, controlled outcomes, cash-versus-stock awards, payment timing, payer source and donation-funded capacity.
sections.qualitative: A selected Massachusetts District Court randomized offer of full representation improved housing retention versus already-unbundled assistance. A companion Housing Court trial found no substantial incremental outcome against forms help and lawyer-for-day assistance. These contrasting trials make alternative aid and client selection decisive; neither measures LSLA health or net dollar resources. Judge-leniency instrumental-variable research in Chicago and NYC links eviction to hospital visits and earnings losses over two years, but estimates eviction consequences rather than legal representation. Earnings are not after-tax consumption and retained housing is not measured QALYs. Current LSLA eligibility may result in advice/brief help rather than full representation. Housing and domestic-violence categories overlap; they are not added as distinct health beneficiaries.
sections.cost: The conditional annual reference changes from $22.50M to $90.05M per better life: 6.513049 health QALYs and -1.690935 signed resource equivalents. Original coefficients with only full-exposure burdens give $59.17M; the subsequent case-scope and additionality judgments give $90.05M. This is a modeling correction/refinement, not evidence whole-portfolio effectiveness fell fourfold. Full matched FY2024 cost remains $43,421,735. N=25,111 case opportunities, unique=.8 and Houston share=.5 are judgments, not observed unique local clients. ClinicalN=12,400 is the reported housing-case envelope rather than an arbitrary quarter of all cases; no separate DV count is added. Additionality .2 replaces .3 as a research-informed mixed-case judgment considering divergent controlled evidence and alternative aid, not an empirical LSLA coefficient. Clinical response .3, utility .02 and two-year persistence remain conditional hypotheses; they are not trial-calibrated QALYs. All 20,088.8 exposed household proxies bear full .0005 QALY harm and $50 access/time burden, independent of additional benefit. Resource successes are 25% of additional households, receiving one-year $2,000 net benefit/settlement resources, $500 disposable work and $100 otherwise-paid care saving. These are hypotheses, not the reported $15.3M awards divided into consumption; property stocks, rent waivers and public-benefit awards differ. Positive components alone receive .5 overlap; negatives and burdens remain full in one joint household log at $20,000 consumption. Work is net of taxes, withdrawn benefits and ordinary work costs. Distinct public/counterparty households bear $1,000 per Houston-attributed success at $50,000 baseline, applied locally once with payer share one; full transfer loss and additional work displacement are stressed. External provider costs attach to all exposed, not only successful cases. Financial-only, clinical-null, adverse, alternative-representation null, short persistence, opportunity costs, no transfer and no-exposure scenarios remain. Missing broader legal/family effects and marginal capacity are unmeasured, not zero. Full annual recipient cost against this partial channel is not complete portfolio EV or an established gift price.
sections.funding: State and federal grants fund most work. Official donation route supports operating EIN 74-1537787, not other justice recipients. Free client eligibility does not establish completed full representation or zero client time costs. This matched 2024 annual reference is not the audited 2025 budget or a verified cost to expand case capacity.

model.costScope: Whole FY 2024 annual legal recipient cost versus one conditional legal-safety and signed-resources channel; not complete portfolio or marginal gift EV.
model.geographicAttribution: 2024 case and housing categories cover broad Texas/Arkansas recipient area; Houston .5 is a judgment, not observed local cases. Counterparty costs allocate local recipient-linked amounts once.
model.formula: exposed=N*unique; incremental=exposed*b; health responders=clinicalN*unique*b*clinicalResponse; health=(responders*q*discounted T - exposed*harm)*g; joint household net resource logs for disjoint successes/other exposed; locally allocated distinct payer loss once; price=10*C/(health+signed income equivalent)
model.counterfactual: Public-funded aid, pro bono and alternative legal providers, self-help, existing benefit eligibility and case resolution retained; only incremental outcomes count.
model.attribution: Mixed-case additionality .2 is judgment informed by contrasting controlled legal-aid regimes; no trial coefficient imported universally. Full client harms/burdens persist without benefit response.
model.uncertainty: Clinical response, utility/persistence, unique households, mixed service dose, net resources, payer mix, Houston share and marginal donation capacity unmeasured.
model.nativeOutcomes: Matched2024 25,111 cases, 12,400+ housing cases, 61,289 individuals and gross awards/savings; not unique incremental outcomes.
